questions.prompt: Morse code represents letters using combinations of which two kinds of signal?
questions.hint: The basic distinction is in the duration of a signal.
questions.explanation: Morse code combines short dots and longer dashes, separated by timed gaps.

questions.explanation: The traditional cell has six positions, arranged in two columns of three. Eight-dot computer braille is a separate extension.

questions.prompt: Why can letter-frequency analysis help attack a simple one-to-one substitution cipher?

choices.text: It preserves how often each substituted symbol occurs
It puts all letters in alphabetical order
It makes every encrypted letter equally common
It leaves the first letter of every word unchanged

questions.hint: A long message can reveal statistical regularities even when no word is readable.
questions.explanation: A fixed substitution relabels letters but preserves their frequency pattern, which can be compared with patterns in the likely language.

questions.prompt: What is the Hamming distance between the bit strings 101101 and 100011?
questions.hint: Compare aligned positions; do not rearrange the bits.
questions.explanation: They differ in the third, fourth and fifth positions, so their Hamming distance is 3.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Independently compared six positions:1=1,0=0,1!=0,1!=0,0!=1,1=1; three differences. XOR101101^100011=001110 has three set bits.

questions.prompt: A data block has one even-parity bit covering the whole block. Which error can escape that parity check?
questions.hint: A single flip changes oddness or evenness; consider what another flip does.
questions.explanation: Flipping two bits leaves the overall parity unchanged, so a single parity check cannot detect that error.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Verified algebraically: XOR parity changes once per flipped bit; an even count of flips cancels. Includes parity bit among checked block bits; only net flips counted.

questions.prompt: What is the basic compression idea behind Huffman coding?

choices.text: Assign the same long code to every symbol
Delete symbols that occur most often
Encrypt common symbols with a second key

questions.hint: Reducing the average length matters more than giving every symbol equal space.
questions.explanation: Huffman coding builds a prefix code whose lengths reflect symbol frequencies, reducing the average bits used per symbol.

questions.prompt: Which set of four binary codewords is prefix-free, so no codeword starts another?
questions.hint: Think of a decoder walking a binary tree and stopping at a leaf for each symbol.
questions.explanation: In 0, 10, 110, 111, none is a prefix of another. Each alternative has a shorter codeword that starts a longer one.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Independently checked all ordered codeword pairs with startsWith; only the first choice has zero prefix collisions.

questions.prompt: Why can no standalone lossless binary code turn every possible 8-bit string into a string shorter than 8 bits?

choices.text: There are fewer distinct shorter outputs than inputs
All short binary strings contain transmission errors
Lossless decoding always requires a secret key

questions.hint: Count possible outputs of lengths zero through seven, including the empty string.
questions.explanation: There are 256 possible inputs but only 1 + 2 + 4 + … + 128 = 255 shorter outputs. At least two inputs would collide, preventing unique recovery.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Original counting proof independently verified sum(2^n,n=0..7)=255<256=2^8. Standalone excludes an external lookup choice or side channel conveying missing information.

questions.prompt: A binary block code has minimum Hamming distance 5. What is the largest number of arbitrary bit errors per block that nearest-codeword decoding is guaranteed to correct?
questions.hint: Error-correction regions around distinct valid codewords must not overlap.
questions.explanation: A minimum distance of 2t + 1 guarantees correction of t errors. With distance 5, t is 2.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Verified bound floor((5-1)/2)=2. Three errors can bring a word closer to another codeword at distance5; claim is guarantee for arbitrary errors.

questions.prompt: Two equal-length messages are XOR-encrypted using the same one-time pad. What does XORing their ciphertexts reveal directly, without knowing the pad?

choices.text: The XOR of the two original messages

questions.hint: XORing any bit with itself cancels it; group the repeated terms.
questions.explanation: If C₁ = M₁ XOR K and C₂ = M₂ XOR K, then C₁ XOR C₂ = M₁ XOR M₂. This leaks a relation between the messages and destroys the pad’s intended secrecy.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Checked lecture’s reused-pad identity. Independently verified associative XOR cancellation K^K=0; does not overclaim that both plaintexts are always immediately recoverable.
